lessons.title: Understanding Multiplication
lessons.description: Understand multiplication as groups of equal objects, repeated addition, and grid arrays. Describe real-world multiplication contexts.

lessons.title: Multiplication on a Number Line
lessons.description: Represent multiplication problems on a number line. Model jumps of equal sizes to calculate products.

lessons.title: Commutative & Associative Properties
lessons.description: Understand commutative (a × b = b × a) and associative properties of multiplication to multiply single-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Understanding Division
lessons.description: Understand division as sharing equally and partition grouping. Interpret quotients as shares or groups.

lessons.title: Multiplication & Division Relationships
lessons.description: Explore the relationship between multiplication and division as inverse operations. Find the missing factor in division families.

lessons.title: Facts for 2s, 5s, and 10s
lessons.description: Develop speed and fluency with multiplication and division facts of 2s, 5s, and 10s using patterns and skip counting.

lessons.title: Facts for 3s, 4s, and 6s
lessons.description: Learn and practice multiplication and division facts for 3s, 4s, and 6s. Develop computational automaticity.

lessons.title: Facts for 7s, 8s, and 9s
lessons.description: Learn and practice multiplication and division facts for 7s, 8s, and 9s. Apply properties and tricks to aid facts recall.

lessons.title: Two-Step Word Problems
lessons.description: Solve two-step word problems involving all four operations. Represent problems with equations and check solutions for reasonableness.

lessons.title: Identifying Arithmetic Patterns
lessons.description: Identify arithmetic patterns in multiplication tables and addition charts. Use mathematical properties to explain patterns.

lessons.title: Rounding Whole Numbers
lessons.description: Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 using place value understanding. Apply rounding in real-world estimation.

lessons.title: Addition & Subtraction within 1000
lessons.description: Fluently add and subtract whole numbers within 1000 using strategies based on place value, properties, and algorithms.

lessons.title: Multiplying by Multiples of 10
lessons.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 (e.g., 9 × 80) using place value understanding and patterns.

lessons.title: Fractions as Parts of a Whole
lessons.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts. Represent parts of a whole.

lessons.title: Fractions on a Number Line
lessons.description: Represent fractions on a number line diagram. Identify unit fraction intervals and plot numbers between 0 and 1.

lessons.title: Equivalent Fractions
lessons.description: Understand fraction equivalence and identify equivalent fractions. Represent whole numbers as fractions (e.g., 3 = 3/1).

lessons.title: Comparing Fractions
lessons.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or same denominator using area models, number lines, and comparisons (<, >, =).

lessons.title: Telling Time & Elapsed Time
lessons.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute. Measure elapsed time intervals in minutes. Solve real-world word problems.

lessons.title: Measuring Liquid Volume & Mass
lessons.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes (liters) and masses (grams, kilograms). Solve word problems using addition and subtraction.

lessons.title: Picture Graphs & Bar Graphs
lessons.description: Draw scaled picture graphs and scaled bar graphs to represent a data set. Solve "how many more" and "how many less" problems.

lessons.title: Measurement Data on Line Plots
lessons.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show data on line plots.

lessons.title: Understanding Area & Unit Squares
lessons.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement. Measure area by counting unit squares.

lessons.title: Area of Rectangles & Decomposing
lessons.description: Relate area to multiplication. Solve real-world area problems for rectangles, apply distributive property, and decompose irregular shapes.

lessons.title: Perimeter & Area Relationships
lessons.description: Solve mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons. Find perimeters given side lengths, find missing sides, and compare areas.

lessons.title: Shape Classes & Financial Literacy
lessons.description: Classify shapes by attributes (e.g., quadrilaterals). Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Understand money, coins, and bills.

questions.prompt: Maya has 4 baskets. She places 5 apples in each basket. How many apples does Maya have in total?
questions.explanation: Maya has 4 groups of 5 apples. 4 × 5 = 20 apples.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiplication represents equal groups of items. Total = (number of groups) × (items in each group).
Strategy Clue: Add 5 four times: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5, or calculate 4 × 5.
Gizmo's Step: Maya has 4 groups of 5 apples. 4 × 5 = 20 apples.

questions.prompt: Which repeated addition sentence represents 3 × 6?
questions.explanation: 3 × 6 means 3 groups with 6 in each group: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.
hints: Concept Rule: 3 × 6 means 3 groups of 6.
Strategy Clue: Write 6 added together 3 times.
Gizmo's Step: 3 × 6 means 3 groups with 6 in each group: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.

questions.prompt: A dog has 4 legs. If there are 6 dogs playing in the dog park, how many total legs are there?
hints: Concept Rule: Multiply the number of items per group by the total number of groups.
Strategy Clue: There are 6 dogs, and each dog has 4 legs. Multiply 6 × 4.
Gizmo's Step: 6 dogs with 4 legs each: 6 × 4 = 24 legs.

questions.prompt: An array has 3 rows of stars with 5 stars in each row. Which multiplication equation models this array?
questions.explanation: An array with 3 rows of 5 stars has 3 × 5 = 15 stars.
hints: Concept Rule: An array arranges objects into equal rows and columns. Total = (rows) × (columns).
Strategy Clue: There are 3 rows and 5 columns.
Gizmo's Step: 3 rows × 5 columns = 15 stars in total.

questions.prompt: Leo planted seeds in an egg carton with 2 rows and 6 columns. How many total seeds did Leo plant?
hints: Concept Rule: To find the total in a grid, multiply the number of rows by the number of columns.
Strategy Clue: Calculate 2 rows × 6 columns.
Gizmo's Step: 2 rows × 6 columns = 12 total seeds.

questions.prompt: Sofia bakes 7 trays of cookies. Each tray holds 4 cookies. How many cookies did Sofia bake in total?
hints: Concept Rule: Total items = (number of trays) × (cookies per tray).
Strategy Clue: Multiply 7 by 4.
Gizmo's Step: 7 trays × 4 cookies per tray = 28 cookies.

questions.prompt: Which story problem represents the equation 5 × 8 = 40?
questions.correctAnswer: Liam bought 5 packs of markers with 8 markers in each pack.

options.text: Liam had 5 markers and found 8 more.
Liam bought 5 packs of markers with 8 markers in each pack.
Liam had 40 markers and gave 8 to a friend.
Liam shared 5 markers equally among 8 friends.

questions.explanation: 5 packs with 8 markers each is 5 equal groups of 8: 5 × 8 = 40.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiplication represents combining equal groups.
Strategy Clue: Look for the situation with 5 equal groups of 8 items.
Gizmo's Step: 5 packs of 8 markers means 5 × 8 = 40 markers.

questions.prompt: A classroom has 8 tables. Each table has 3 chairs. How many chairs are in the classroom altogether?
hints: Concept Rule: Multiply the number of groups by the size of each group.
Strategy Clue: Multiply 8 tables by 3 chairs per table.
Gizmo's Step: 8 tables × 3 chairs = 24 chairs.

questions.prompt: A frog starts at 0 and takes 4 jumps of size 3 on a number line. At what number does the frog land?
hints: Concept Rule: Jumping on a number line models multiplication: (number of jumps) × (jump size).
Strategy Clue: Calculate 4 × 3.
Gizmo's Step: 4 jumps of 3 = 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.prompt: A grasshopper takes 5 jumps of size 2 on a number line. Which equation models these jumps?
questions.explanation: 5 jumps of size 2 is represented by 5 × 2 = 10.
hints: Concept Rule: The number of jumps is the first factor; the jump size is the second factor.
Strategy Clue: 5 jumps of 2 units each equals 5 × 2.
Gizmo's Step: 5 jumps of 2 lands on 10, so 5 × 2 = 10.

questions.prompt: A rabbit jumps from 0 to 18 on a number line by making equal jumps of 6. How many jumps did the rabbit make?
hints: Concept Rule: Divide the ending number by the size of each jump: (Total distance) ÷ (jump size) = (number of jumps).
Strategy Clue: Calculate 18 ÷ 6.
Gizmo's Step: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 jumps of size 6.

questions.prompt: Kiran makes 6 jumps of size 4 on a number line. What is Kiran's landing point?
hints: Concept Rule: Landing point = (jumps) × (jump size).
Strategy Clue: Multiply 6 by 4.
Gizmo's Step: 6 jumps of 4 units = 6 × 4 = 24.

questions.prompt: On a number line, if you start at 0 and make 7 jumps of 5, what number do you reach?
hints: Concept Rule: Skip count by 5 seven times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35.
Strategy Clue: 7 × 5 = 35.
Gizmo's Step: 7 jumps of 5 is 7 × 5 = 35.

questions.prompt: A cricket makes 8 jumps of size 4 on a number line starting at 0. Where is the cricket now?
hints: Concept Rule: Multiply the number of jumps by the distance per jump.
Strategy Clue: 8 jumps of 4 = 8 × 4.
Gizmo's Step: 8 × 4 = 32 on the number line.

questions.prompt: Which number line jump pattern shows 9 × 3 = 27?
hints: Concept Rule: The first number is the number of jumps, and the second is the jump length.
Strategy Clue: 9 jumps of 3 units equals 27.
Gizmo's Step: 9 jumps of 3 starting at 0 models 9 × 3 = 27.

questions.prompt: If you make jumps of size 7 starting at 0 and reach 42, how many jumps did you make?
hints: Concept Rule: To find the number of jumps: (final number) ÷ (jump size).
Strategy Clue: Calculate 42 ÷ 7.
Gizmo's Step: Calculate 42 ÷ 7. Completing this step confirms the result is 6.

questions.prompt: According to the Commutative Property of Multiplication, if 4 × 7 = 28, then 7 × 4 = ?
hints: Concept Rule: The Commutative Property states that changing the order of factors does not change the product: a × b = b × a.
Strategy Clue: 4 × 7 has the same product as 7 × 4.
Gizmo's Step: By the Commutative Property, 7 × 4 = 4 × 7 = 28.

questions.prompt: Which equation illustrates the Commutative Property of Multiplication?
hints: Concept Rule: The Commutative Property of Multiplication switches the order of factors in multiplication.
Strategy Clue: Look for multiplication where the numbers swap places across the equals sign.
Gizmo's Step: 3 × 8 = 8 × 3 is the Commutative Property of Multiplication.

questions.prompt: Use the Associative Property: (2 × 3) × 5 = 2 × (3 × 5). What is the product?
hints: Concept Rule: The Associative Property states that grouping factors differently does not change the product: (a × b) × c = a × (b × c).
Strategy Clue: Calculate inside first: 2 × 3 = 6, then 6 × 5 = 30; or 3 × 5 = 15, then 2 × 15 = 30.

questions.prompt: What number makes this equation true: (4 × 2) × 3 = 4 × (? × 3)?
questions.explanation: By the Associative Property, the missing factor is 2.
hints: Concept Rule: The Associative Property regroups the exact same factors: (a × b) × c = a × (b × c).
Strategy Clue: Compare the factors: 4, 2, and 3 are in both expressions.
Gizmo's Step: By the Associative Property, the missing factor is 2.

questions.prompt: Calculate (5 × 2) × 7 using mental math by grouping 5 × 2 first. What is the result?
hints: Concept Rule: Multiply (5 × 2) first to get an easy multiple of 10.
Strategy Clue: 5 × 2 = 10. Now multiply 10 × 7.

questions.prompt: If 9 × 6 = 54, find the missing number in: 6 × ___ = 54.
hints: Concept Rule: Commutative property: a × b = b × a.
Strategy Clue: Since 9 × 6 = 54, then 6 × 9 = 54.
Gizmo's Step: By the Commutative Property, 6 × 9 = 54.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is equal to 4 × (2 × 5)?
hints: Concept Rule: The Associative Property allows changing parentheses grouping in multiplication.
Strategy Clue: 4 × (2 × 5) = (4 × 2) × 5.
Gizmo's Step: (4 × 2) × 5 = 8 × 5 = 40, which matches 4 × 10 = 40.

questions.prompt: Calculate (3 × 3) × 4. What is the value?
hints: Concept Rule: Evaluate inside parentheses first, then multiply by the remaining factor.
Strategy Clue: 3 × 3 = 9, then multiply 9 × 4.

questions.prompt: A teacher shares 15 crayons equally among 3 students. How many crayons does each student receive?
hints: Concept Rule: Division is equal sharing: (total items) ÷ (number of groups) = (items per group).
Strategy Clue: Calculate 15 ÷ 3.
Gizmo's Step: 15 crayons divided among 3 students: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 crayons.

questions.prompt: There are 18 cookies. Mom puts 3 cookies into each bag. How many bags does she fill?
hints: Concept Rule: Division by grouping: (total items) ÷ (items in each group) = (number of groups).
Strategy Clue: Divide 18 by 3.
Gizmo's Step: Divide 18 by 3. Completing this step confirms the result is 6 bags.

questions.prompt: Marcus has 24 stickers. He puts an equal number on each of 4 pages. How many stickers are on each page?
hints: Concept Rule: Divide total stickers by the number of pages.
Strategy Clue: Calculate 24 ÷ 4.
Gizmo's Step: 24 stickers ÷ 4 pages = 6 stickers per page.

questions.prompt: Which division equation represents sharing 20 marbles equally among 5 friends?
hints: Concept Rule: Total items is the dividend (first number), groups is the divisor (second number).
Strategy Clue: 20 shared among 5 friends is written as 20 ÷ 5.
Gizmo's Step: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 represents 20 marbles shared among 5 friends.

questions.prompt: Solve: 28 ÷ 7.
hints: Concept Rule: Think of multiplication: What number times 7 equals 28?
Strategy Clue: 7 × 4 = 28, so 28 ÷ 7 = 4.
Gizmo's Step: 7 × 4 = 28, so 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Completing this step confirms the result is 4.

questions.prompt: A baker packs 36 muffins into boxes of 6. How many boxes of muffins does the baker make?
hints: Concept Rule: Divide total muffins by muffins per box.
Strategy Clue: Calculate 36 ÷ 6.
Gizmo's Step: Calculate 36 ÷ 6. Completing this step confirms the result is 6.

questions.prompt: If you have 35 tennis balls and put 5 balls into each can, which equation tells you the number of cans?
hints: Concept Rule: Find how many equal groups of 5 are in 35.
Strategy Clue: 35 divided by 5 equals 7.
Gizmo's Step: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 is the correct division equation.

questions.prompt: There are 40 students going on a field trip. If 4 students ride in each van, how many vans are needed?
hints: Concept Rule: Divide the total number of students by the number per van.
Strategy Clue: 40 ÷ 4 = 10.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 10, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number in the fact family: 6 × ___ = 42.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiplication and division are inverse operations. If 6 × ? = 42, then 42 ÷ 6 = ?.
Strategy Clue: Calculate 42 ÷ 6.
Gizmo's Step: 6 × 7 = 42, so the missing number is 7.

questions.prompt: Which equation belongs to the same fact family as 4 × 8 = 32?
questions.explanation: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 is an inverse relationship in the fact family.
hints: Concept Rule: A fact family consists of related facts using the same three numbers (4, 8, 32).
Strategy Clue: The related division equations are 32 ÷ 8 = 4 and 32 ÷ 4 = 8.
Gizmo's Step: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 belongs to this fact family.

questions.prompt: What is the missing value: ___ ÷ 5 = 9?
hints: Concept Rule: To find the dividend, multiply the divisor by the quotient: ? = 5 × 9.
Strategy Clue: Calculate 5 × 9.
Gizmo's Step: 45 ÷ 5 = 9, so the missing value is 45.

questions.prompt: Find the unknown factor: 8 × ___ = 64.
hints: Concept Rule: Divide 64 by 8 to find the unknown factor.
Strategy Clue: 64 ÷ 8 = 8.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 8, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: If you know that 7 × 9 = 63, what is 63 ÷ 7?
hints: Concept Rule: Multiplication and division undo each other.
Strategy Clue: Since 7 × 9 = 63, 63 ÷ 7 must be 9.
Gizmo's Step: Since 7 × 9 = 63, 63 ÷ 7 must be 9. Completing this step confirms the result is 9.

questions.prompt: Find the value of k in: 54 ÷ k = 6.
hints: Concept Rule: Think: 6 × k = 54. What number times 6 gives 54?
Strategy Clue: 54 ÷ 6 = 9.
Gizmo's Step: 54 ÷ 9 = 6, so k = 9.

questions.prompt: Which number sentence can help you solve 48 ÷ 6 = ___?
hints: Concept Rule: Division can be solved as an unknown-factor multiplication problem.
Strategy Clue: 48 ÷ 6 = ? means 6 × ? = 48.
Gizmo's Step: 6 × ___ = 48 is the corresponding multiplication sentence.

questions.prompt: Solve for n: n × 7 = 56.
hints: Concept Rule: Divide 56 by 7 to find n.
Strategy Clue: 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
Gizmo's Step: 8 × 7 = 56, so n = 8.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 7 × 2.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiplying by 2 means doubling the number.
Strategy Clue: 7 + 7 = 14.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 14, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Which product is equal to 9 × 5?
hints: Concept Rule: Multiples of 5 always end in 0 or 5.
Strategy Clue: Count by 5 nine times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45.
Gizmo's Step: Count by 5 nine times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. Completing this step confirms the result is 45.

questions.prompt: Solve: 8 × 10.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiplying a whole number by 10 appends a 0 to the ones place.
Strategy Clue: 8 with a 0 at the end is 80.
Gizmo's Step: 8 with a 0 at the end is 80. Completing this step confirms the result is 80.

questions.prompt: What is 50 ÷ 5?
hints: Concept Rule: Think: 5 times what number equals 50?
Strategy Clue: 5 × 10 = 50.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 10, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Solve: 18 ÷ 2.
hints: Concept Rule: Dividing by 2 is cutting in half.
Strategy Clue: Half of 18 is 9.
Gizmo's Step: Half of 18 is 9. Completing this step confirms the result is 9.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 6 × 5.
hints: Concept Rule: Skip count by 5 six times.
Strategy Clue: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.
Gizmo's Step: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Completing this step confirms the result is 30.

questions.prompt: What is 70 ÷ 10?
hints: Concept Rule: Dividing by 10 removes a zero from the ones place.
Strategy Clue: 70 ÷ 10 = 7.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 7, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 12 × 5.
hints: Concept Rule: Break 12 into (10 + 2): (10 × 5) + (2 × 5).
Strategy Clue: 50 + 10 = 60.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 60, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 6 × 3.
hints: Concept Rule: Count by 3 six times or count by 6 three times.
Strategy Clue: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.
Gizmo's Step: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. Completing this step confirms the result is 18.

questions.prompt: What is 7 × 4?
hints: Concept Rule: To multiply by 4, double the number twice.
Strategy Clue: Double 7 is 14; double 14 is 28.
Gizmo's Step: Double 7 is 14; double 14 is 28. Completing this step confirms the result is 28.

questions.prompt: Solve: 9 × 4.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiply 9 by 4: double 9 is 18, double 18 is 36.
Strategy Clue: 9 × 4 = 36.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 36, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: What is 24 ÷ 6?
hints: Concept Rule: Think: 6 × ? = 24.
Strategy Clue: 6 × 4 = 24.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 4, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Solve: 36 ÷ 4.
hints: Concept Rule: Think: 4 times what equals 36?
Strategy Clue: 4 × 9 = 36.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 9, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 8 × 6.
hints: Concept Rule: Use 8 × 5 = 40, then add one more 8.
Strategy Clue: 40 + 8 = 48.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 48, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: What is 27 ÷ 3?
hints: Concept Rule: Think: 3 × ? = 27.
Strategy Clue: 3 × 9 = 27.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 9, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 7 × 6.
hints: Concept Rule: Use 7 × 5 = 35 and add 7.
Strategy Clue: 35 + 7 = 42.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 42, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 7 × 7.
hints: Concept Rule: 7 squared equals 49.
Strategy Clue: 7 groups of 7 = 49.
Gizmo's Step: 7 groups of 7 = 49. Completing this step confirms the result is 49.

questions.prompt: What is 8 × 7?
hints: Concept Rule: Remember the sequence: 5, 6, 7, 8 -> 56 = 7 × 8.
Strategy Clue: 7 × 8 = 56.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 56, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 9 × 8.
hints: Concept Rule: For 9 facts, the digits add up to 9: 7 + 2 = 9.
Strategy Clue: 10 × 8 = 80, subtract 8 = 72.
Gizmo's Step: 10 × 8 = 80, subtract 8 = 72. Completing this step confirms the result is 72.

questions.prompt: What is 63 ÷ 7?
hints: Concept Rule: Think: 7 × ? = 63.
Strategy Clue: 7 × 9 = 63.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 9, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Solve: 81 ÷ 9.
hints: Concept Rule: 9 × 9 = 81.
Strategy Clue: 81 divided by 9 equals 9.
Gizmo's Step: 81 divided by 9 equals 9. Completing this step confirms the result is 9.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 9 × 9.
hints: Concept Rule: 9 squared equals 81.
Strategy Clue: 10 × 9 = 90, subtract 9 = 81.
Gizmo's Step: 10 × 9 = 90, subtract 9 = 81. Completing this step confirms the result is 81.

hints: Concept Rule: 8 × 8 = 64.
Strategy Clue: 64 ÷ 8 = 8.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 8, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Calculate: 8 × 8.
hints: Concept Rule: 8 squared equals 64.
Strategy Clue: 8 × 8 = 64.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 64, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: Chloe bought 3 packs of gum with 5 pieces in each pack. She chewed 4 pieces. How many pieces of gum are left?
hints: Concept Rule: Two-step problem: First multiply to find the total, then subtract the chewed pieces.
Strategy Clue: Step 1: 3 × 5 = 15 pieces. Step 2: 15 - 4.
Gizmo's Step: Total gum = 3 × 5 = 15. Remaining = 15 - 4 = 11 pieces.

questions.prompt: Maya has 4 boxes with 6 crayons each. Her teacher gives her 8 more crayons. How many crayons does Maya have now?
hints: Concept Rule: First find crayons in boxes (4 × 6), then add the extra crayons (+ 8).
Strategy Clue: 4 × 6 = 24. 24 + 8 = 32.
Gizmo's Step: 4 × 6 = 24 crayons in boxes. 24 + 8 = 32 crayons altogether.

questions.prompt: A bakery baked 50 muffins. They sold 26 muffins in the morning and 14 muffins in the afternoon. How many muffins are left?
hints: Concept Rule: Find the total muffins sold by adding morning and afternoon sales, then subtract from 50.
Strategy Clue: 26 + 14 = 40 sold. 50 - 40 = ?
Gizmo's Step: Total sold = 26 + 14 = 40. Remaining = 50 - 40 = 10 muffins.

questions.prompt: Jake had $40. He bought 3 books that cost $7 each. How much money does Jake have left?
hints: Concept Rule: First multiply 3 books by $7 to get total cost. Then subtract cost from $40.
Gizmo's Step: Cost of books = 3 × $7 = $21. Remaining money = $40 - $21 = $19.

questions.prompt: Emma has 2 bags with 8 apples in each bag. She shares all of her apples equally among 4 friends. How many apples does each friend get?
questions.explanation: Total apples = 2 × 8 = 16. Apples per friend = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 apples.
hints: Concept Rule: Step 1: Total apples = 2 × 8. Step 2: Divide total by 4 friends.
Strategy Clue: 2 × 8 = 16 apples. 16 ÷ 4 = ?
Gizmo's Step: Total apples = 2 × 8 = 16. Apples per friend = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 apples.

questions.prompt: A grocer puts 5 boxes of apples on display with 6 apples in each box. If 3 apples are damaged and removed, how many apples are left?
hints: Concept Rule: Find total apples first (5 × 6), then subtract the 3 damaged apples.
Strategy Clue: 5 × 6 = 30. 30 - 3 = 27.
Gizmo's Step: 5 × 6 = 30 apples. 30 - 3 = 27 good apples.

questions.prompt: Noah collected 18 shells. His brother collected 14 shells. They put all of their shells equally into 4 jars. How many shells are in each jar?
hints: Concept Rule: First add all shells (18 + 14 = 32), then divide by 4 jars.
Strategy Clue: 18 + 14 = 32 shells. 32 ÷ 4 = 8 shells.
Gizmo's Step: Total shells = 18 + 14 = 32. Per jar = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 shells.

questions.prompt: 4 baskets have 8 oranges each. If 12 oranges are squeezed to make fresh juice, how many oranges remain?
hints: Concept Rule: Calculate total oranges: 4 × 8 = 32. Subtract oranges used: 32 - 12.
Strategy Clue: 32 - 12 = 20 oranges.
Gizmo's Step: Total oranges = 4 × 8 = 32. Remaining = 32 - 12 = 20 oranges.

questions.prompt: What is the next number in the arithmetic pattern: 4, 8, 12, 16, ___?
questions.explanation: The pattern increases by 4 each term. 16 + 4 = 20.
hints: Concept Rule: Find the rule: subtract consecutive terms to find the step size.
Strategy Clue: 8 - 4 = 4; the pattern adds 4 each time. 16 + 4 = ?
Gizmo's Step: The pattern increases by 4 each term. 16 + 4 = 20.

questions.prompt: When you multiply any whole number by an even number, what kind of product do you always get?
questions.explanation: Multiplying any number by an even number always produces an even number.
hints: Concept Rule: Even numbers have 2 as a factor. Any multiple of an even number also has 2 as a factor.
Strategy Clue: Try examples: 3 × 2 = 6 (even), 5 × 4 = 20 (even).
Gizmo's Step: Try examples: 3 × 2 = 6 (even), 5 × 4 = 20 (even). Completing this step confirms the result is An even number.

questions.prompt: In the addition pattern, adding two odd numbers always gives an even number. What is the sum of 5 + 7?
hints: Concept Rule: Odd + Odd = Even.
Strategy Clue: 5 + 7 = 12.
Gizmo's Step: Working through the calculation gives 12, verifying the solution step by step.

questions.prompt: What is the rule for the pattern: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30?
questions.explanation: Each term is 6 greater than the previous term, so the rule is Add 6.
hints: Concept Rule: Check the difference between consecutive numbers: 12 - 6 = 6, 18 - 12 = 6.
Strategy Clue: The rule adds 6 each time.
Gizmo's Step: Each term is 6 greater than the previous term, so the rule is Add 6.

questions.prompt: What is the next number in the pattern of multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, ___?
hints: Concept Rule: Add 9 to the last number: 36 + 9.
Strategy Clue: 36 + 9 = 45.
Gizmo's Step: Multiples of 9 increase by 9. 36 + 9 = 45.

questions.prompt: What is the next number in this decreasing pattern: 100, 90, 80, 70, ___?
hints: Concept Rule: Each step subtracts 10.
Strategy Clue: 70 - 10 = 60.
Gizmo's Step: The rule is subtract 10. 70 - 10 = 60.

questions.prompt: Which of the following numbers belongs to the pattern of multiples of 4?
questions.explanation: 28 = 4 × 7, so it belongs to the pattern of multiples of 4.
hints: Concept Rule: Multiples of 4 are divisible by 4 with no remainder.
Strategy Clue: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 with no remainder.
Gizmo's Step: 28 = 4 × 7, so it belongs to the pattern of multiples of 4.

questions.prompt: What is the missing number in the pattern: 3, 7, 11, ___, 19?
hints: Concept Rule: Find the difference: 7 - 3 = 4, 11 - 7 = 4. The pattern adds 4.
